---
title: "Stage 12 – Your own project"
---
The route ends on a project of your own. You choose one of the four cases and ask a question beyond the claim that SCORE selected from its paper, one that the data of the case support: another claim or outcome of the paper, an option that the menu of the case sets aside because it answers a different question, the later surveys that the data hold, or a replication on new data. The [list below](#the-projects) gives the projects that each case supports and where to start. The project follows the rule of every case report, with one addition. Its preregistration is complete before anything in it runs, and it is also fixed with a date that someone else can check, either as the first commit of the repository of the project, pushed to GitHub, or as a registration on OSF Registries. This stage therefore begins with version control, then writes and commits the preregistration, runs the declared analysis and prepares the work for an archive. It is the longest stage of the route, about six and a quarter hours of work, and is best spread over several sittings.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Git and GitHub for reproducible research](../../companion/git-github.qmd), from [Version control](../../companion/git-github.qmd#sec-why) to [GitHub](../../companion/git-github.qmd#sec-github) | Version control from first principles; git on your own machine, with staging, committing, the log and the diffs, and the source-control pane of your IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.); then GitHub, remotes, the README, and forks, templates and pull requests. | 90 minutes |
| [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-prereg-templates), registrations and preregistration templates | The two templates that the module describes, the AsPredicted form and the template for secondary data. Write the preregistration of your project with one of them, with a data-in-hand statement that says what you have already looked at in the data. Make it the first commit of a new repository and push it to GitHub, or register it on OSF Registries, before you run anything. | 75 minutes |
| [Git and GitHub for reproducible research](../../companion/git-github.qmd), [What to track](../../companion/git-github.qmd#sec-repro) and [Your own reanalysis](../../companion/git-github.qmd#sec-application) | What belongs in a repository and what never does, with the licensed Eurobarometer files as the example of what stays out; then your own reanalysis under version control, one decision per commit. Add the four case reports with the workspaces that render them. The `.gitignore` files of the immigration-and-trust and EU-frames workspaces keep out their `data_private/` folders, which hold the file of the analysts and your respondent file. | 50 minutes |
| Your project | Run the specification that you declared, and that one first; report its result as your preregistration said you would, and place it beside the curve of the case where it can be placed. Label anything that you add after seeing the result as exploratory. Commit as you go. | 130 minutes |
| [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd#sec-deposit), depositing a reanalysis of your own | A route for depositing a reanalysis: the code on a forge, each version archived with a DOI, the data where their licence allows and nowhere else, and the plan on the OSF with the identifiers of the rest. Write the README of your repository by it. | 30 minutes |
| Optional: [Quarto and reproducible documents](../../companion/quarto.qmd), [Projects](../../companion/quarto.qmd#sec-project) and [Publishing the document](../../companion/quarto.qmd#sec-publish) | The four case reports and the project rendered together as one Quarto project, and the rendered output published where other people can reach it. | as you like |

**Shortcuts.** If you already use git and GitHub, skip the first row and read [What to track](../../companion/git-github.qmd#sec-repro) for what the licences of the four cases keep out of a repository.

**By the end of the stage** you have a repository whose first commit is the preregistration of your project as you wrote it, which holds the four case reports and the project, which leaves out every licensed survey file, and which another person can clone and re-render by following its README; and you have the declared analysis of your project run and reported.

## The projects {#the-projects}

Each row names a direction that the data and the pages of the case support. The question, the specification and the rule by which the result is judged are yours to declare.

| Case | Beyond the claim | Where to start |
|---|---|---|
| Housing audit | Another outcome of the paper, whether officials replied at all or replied within 24 hours, or the Black names against the white names, all in `housing_audit.csv`. | [Other outcomes and the Black names](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#outcomes) on the Multiverse page |
| Housing audit | A subgroup, the male or the female names alone, or the officials with Hispanic names, a question about representative bureaucracy asked of a group selected after the emails arrived. | [Subgroups](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#subgroups) and [Who replied](../../cases/housing/menu.qmd#who-replied) on the menu |
| Housing audit | A replication on new data: the preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities that SCORE ran, whose de-identified data, do-file and dictionary are public, analysed with the decisions of the menu. | [The replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) in the case study, and the data at [osf.io/xseqg](https://osf.io/xseqg/) |
| Immigration and trust | Everyone in the extract, with the non-citizens and the members of ethnic minorities whom the paper leaves out. | [Respondents](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#respondents) on the menu |
| Immigration and trust | The interaction of concern with the long-term countries of immigration in Table 4 of the paper, which the file of the analysts coded the wrong way round; the course data carry the country variable in `trust_macro.csv`. | [The file of the analysts](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-analyst-file) in the case study |
| Immigration and trust | Trust in political parties or in the European Parliament, or the claim on rounds 5 and later of the ESS, which needs the full files from the ESS Data Portal after registration. | [The three trust items](../../companion/measurement.qmd#sec-trust-outcome) in the module on scales, and [the replications](../../cases/trust/index.qmd#sec-replication) in the case study |
| Cohabitation | The same comparison on other surveys that the union file holds, from 2002 to 2013–2015, or separation in place of marriage as the outcome. | [Surveys compared](../../cases/cohabitation/menu.qmd#comparison) and [Outcome](../../cases/cohabitation/menu.qmd#outcome) on the menu, and [Other surveys](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd#sec-surveys) on the Multiverse page |
| Cohabitation | The main finding of the paper, the change by education, which is the interaction that SCORE tested in its replication. | [The groups behind the claim](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd#sec-subgroups) on the Multiverse page, and [the replications](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-replication) in the case study |
| Cohabitation | The surveys of the NSFG after 2015, built from the public-use files in the way in which the course built its union file. | [Codebook of the union file](../../cases/cohabitation/data/cohab_unions_codebook.md) |
| EU frames | The other half of the first hypothesis of the paper, a rise in negative framing, on the negative scales. | [The negative scales](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#negative-scales) on the Multiverse page |
| EU frames | A different estimand: the average European in place of the average member state, with the population weight, or the years before the crisis, the crisis years, or the member states without the bailout countries. | [The average European](../../companion/weighting.qmd#the-average-european) in the module on weights, and [heterogeneity and influence](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-heterogeneity) in the multiverse module |
| EU frames | The second claim of the paper, on the gap between education groups, on the simulated respondents of the course or on the respondent file that you built in stage 10, which never leaves your machine. | [Claim 2](../../companion/individual-level.qmd#sec-claim2) in the module on the individual level, and [the panel by education band](../../companion/data-management.qmd#sec-edu) |
| EU frames | The claim on later Eurobarometer waves, such as those of 2013 to 2019 on which the SCORE replication tested it, with the data built by you from the files at GESIS by the route of stage 10. The course has no unit on these waves. | [The replication](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-repetition) in the case study, [the Eurobarometer microdata at GESIS](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the data-sources module, and [Building the analysis file](../../companion/data-management.qmd) |
